fields.title: Cost and Margin
fields.keyTakeaway: Unit cost must fall with scale, and if it does not, the reason is usually external services, and the levers there are product and negotiation, not technical.
fields.sections/0/blocks/0/text: How does an architectural decision reflect in gross margin?
fields.sections/1/blocks/0/text: A product can grow in revenue and not grow in profit if unit cost grows alongside volume. This is usually discovered late—when growth has already happened.
fields.sections/2/blocks/0/text: [[gross-margin|Gross margin]] is the share of revenue after direct costs. Infrastructure and external services are direct costs, and they enter it directly.
fields.sections/2/blocks/1/text: Key question: **does unit cost grow with volume or fall?**
fields.sections/2/blocks/2/text: *Falls*—[[economies-of-scale|economies of scale]]: [[fixed-variable-costs|fixed costs]] are spread across a larger number of users. Good sign.
fields.sections/2/blocks/3/text: *Does not change*—costs are purely variable. Neutral.
fields.sections/2/blocks/4/text: *Grows*—alarming sign. Usually means something scales non-linearly: data accumulates, requests get more complex with volume growth, more expensive architecture is required.
fields.sections/2/blocks/5/text: Product decisions affecting margin through infrastructure:
fields.sections/2/blocks/6/text: *Action frequency.* A function called on every open is more expensive than one called on click. *Stored volume.* Retention period from `DS2-N6` is a direct cost line. *External services.* The most expensive part because the unit price is fixed and does not drop with scale. *Data freshness.* A real-time requirement is multiple times more expensive than an hour delay.
fields.sections/2/blocks/7/text: The latter is often underestimated: the product requirement "real-time" can cost more than the rest of the feature.
fields.sections/3/blocks/0/text: Cost dynamics per active user over a year: 9.1 → 8.4 → 7.9 → 7.5 RUB. Falling—economies of scale are working.
fields.sections/3/blocks/1/text: The breakdown showed that the compute part is falling, while external calls per user are stable. With a threefold growth, the share of external calls in costs will grow from 23% to 38%.
fields.sections/3/blocks/2/text: Hence the strategic conclusion: **further reduction of unit cost rests on external services,** and the levers there are negotiation (volume discounts) and product (calling less frequently), not technical.
fields.sections/3/blocks/3/text: Commission calculation: at an average check of 2,400 and a 4% commission, revenue per order is 96 RUB, direct costs 35 RUB, gross margin 64%. Out of 35 RUB, 29 RUB is the payment provider commission. Negotiations to lower it from 1.2% to 0.9% would yield more than any infrastructure optimization.
fields.sections/4/blocks/0/text: Gross margin does not account for the team and development—the largest item for most products. Infrastructure savings make sense when comparable to these costs.
fields.sections/5/blocks/0/text: Unit cost must fall with scale, and if it does not, the reason is usually external services, and the levers there are product and negotiation, not technical.
